headline: Dengue risk to surge in 15 districts across Bangladesh in coming weeks
summary: The government's IEDCR predicts a worsening situation in late September and early October, with a nationwide prevention campaign launching this Saturday.
details: Dengue has spread to all 64 districts of Bangladesh, with hundreds of people being hospitalized daily. Preventable deaths are occurring almost every day due to this mosquito-borne disease.
The government warns that the Dengue situation will worsen in late September and early October. At least 15 districts are expected to see a further increase in infections during this period.

In response, the government is launching a nationwide Dengue prevention and cleanliness campaign starting this Saturday. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will inaugurate the program from the South Plaza of the National Parliament.
The campaign is expected to run for three months, involving 3-4 ministries, volunteers, and various officials. Students are also encouraged to clean their institutions as part of this initiative.

The Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR), after analyzing data, identified Dhaka, Khulna, Chattogram, Gazipur, Mymensingh, Pirojpur, Narayanganj, Jhalokati, Cox's Bazar, Sirajganj, Cumilla, Barishal, Barguna, Bandarban, and Patuakhali as high-risk districts.

Public health experts and entomologists have been warning for months about the risk of a worsening Dengue situation in September-October. State Minister for Health M. A. Muhith confirmed that cases are rising and the peak is expected soon.
Experts criticize the current situation as preventable, noting that Kolkata in West Bengal, India, has Dengue under control despite similar geographical and environmental conditions.

A major Dengue outbreak first hit Dhaka in 2000, primarily affecting large cities like Dhaka and Chattogram annually. In 2019, the disease spread nationwide for the first time, becoming a permanent public health issue due to a lack of scientific mosquito control and effective public awareness over the past two and a half decades.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reported two Dengue deaths yesterday. This brings the total Dengue fatalities this year to 141, with 49,220 people hospitalized so far.

Analysis of government data shows an increasing trend in deaths, with monthly infections consistently rising from May to September. Division-wise data indicates Khulna Division has the highest number of cases and deaths after Dhaka.
Government data also reveals that 62% of those infected are male, while 38% are female. However, 52% of the total deaths are women, and 48% are men.

IEDCR analyzed Dengue data up to September 5, 2023, noting that the mortality rate this year is currently low at 0.29% as of yesterday. However, 2023 is projected to see the highest number of cases (321,179) and deaths (1,705) in the country's history, with a projected mortality rate of 0.53%.
IEDCR also found that 91.5% of infections this year are caused by Dengue serotype DENV3, and 8.5% by DENV2. DENV2 is responsible for infections in Barguna, Bandarban, and Pirojpur districts.

Epidemiologists explain that Dengue has four serotypes (DENV1, DENV2, DENV3, DENV4). Infection with one serotype provides immunity against that specific type, but individuals remain at risk of infection from the other three.

headline_marked: [[Process begins to recruit 5,000 doctors]] for public hospitals nationwide
headline: Process begins to recruit 5,000 doctors for public hospitals nationwide
summary: The initiative aims to address the severe shortage of medical professionals in government hospitals, especially at the grassroots level, improving healthcare access across the country.
details: Bangladesh Public Service Commission (PSC) has initiated the process to recruit 5,000 new doctors through a special BCS. This move aims to alleviate the existing shortage of medical professionals in government hospitals across the country.

Of the total, 4,700 doctors will be appointed as Assistant Surgeons or Medical Officers, while the remaining 300 will fill Dental Surgeon positions. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has already sent a formal request to the PSC to expedite the recruitment.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), there are currently 11,495 vacant doctor positions against 41,806 approved posts in public hospitals. The World Health Organization (WHO) standards suggest Bangladesh needs approximately 88,909 doctors.

The Finance Minister, in the 2026-27 budget speech, emphasized enhancing healthcare capacity and ensuring medical services reach the grassroots level. The health sector received a record allocation of BDT 69,409 crore, representing 1.01% of the GDP.

PSC Senior Member Sujayet Ullah confirmed receiving the demand letter and stated that the commission will publish the official special BCS circular very soon, following existing regulations. Special BCS exams typically involve only preliminary and oral tests, allowing for quicker recruitment.

Meanwhile, Professor Mohammad Nazmuzzaman Bhuiyan has taken charge as the new PSC Chairman, having sworn in on September 6. He affirmed his commitment to fulfilling his constitutional duties with diligence, transparency, and integrity.

This recruitment follows a previous initiative in May 2025, when 3,000 doctors were appointed through the 48th special BCS. The new intake of 5,000 doctors is expected to significantly improve quality healthcare, particularly in upazila health complexes and rural areas.
